# <a id="_qkjomrof9agi"></a>__The Great Contact Lens Caper of the 70s__

[JANET RILEY](https://substack.com/@juanita4141)

Jan 18, 2026

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

Back in the 1970s, before disposable plastic lenses became the norm, contact lenses were a luxury—hard, tiny, and incredibly expensive\. My sister, ever the trendsetter, refused to wear glasses and insisted on contacts, a decision that often led to spontaneous, high\-stakes scavenger hunts\. These tiny brown discs had a mischievous habit of popping out at the most inconvenient times: in a grassy field, on a busy sidewalk, or just, inexplicably, mid\-stride\. Losing one was not just an inconvenience; it was a minor financial crisis\.

One fateful evening, with a cousin visiting, we decided to make the most of the dwindling daylight by heading to the local schoolyard\. Swings, slides, and monkey bars beckoned, promising an hour of carefree play\. What we didn’t know was that the school had recently experienced a break\-in\. So, when a few observant neighbors spotted three figures lingering around the playground equipment as dusk began to fall, their imaginations, fueled by recent events, took flight\. They saw not innocent children, but potential culprits, and quickly dialed the police\.

Just as the sky was turning a deep indigo and it was time for us to head home, my sister let out the dreaded cry: “My contact popped out\!” Immediately, our carefree evening transformed into an urgent search mission\. The three of us dropped to our hands and knees, frantically sifting through the gritty playground sand and scattered pebbles, trying to locate that almost\-invisible, tiny brown disc\.

It was in this absurd tableau—three kids crawling around a darkening playground, searching for a contact lens—that we saw them\. Three police officers, their silhouettes growing larger against the fading light, were striding purposefully towards us\. One of them carried the most enormous flashlight I had ever seen, its beam cutting through the twilight like a searchlight\.

My heart pounded\. *Oh my gosh, am I going to get arrested? What are they going to do to us?* The playground, once a place of joy, suddenly felt like the scene of a crime\.

“What are you doing here?” one of the officers asked, his voice firm, the beam of the flashlight sweeping over us\.

We stammered out our unlikely truth: “We’re looking for my sister’s contact lens\!”

To our immense relief, the tension visibly eased\. The officer with the giant flashlight, a hero in uniform, got down on his knees with us\. With the power of his industrial\-strength beam, he meticulously scanned the ground\. And then, a miracle\! He spotted it—the elusive brown contact lens, nestled among the grains of sand\. He carefully picked it up, handed it to my relieved sister, and then, with a smile that was both stern and understanding, said, “Alright, you kids need to get going\. Time to go home\.”

We didn’t need to be told twice\. We practically sprinted all the way back to our very nice suburban home, our hearts still thumping from the unexpected encounter\. My cousin, overwhelmed by the entire ordeal, spent the rest of the evening on my mom’s lap, finding solace in the entire contents of the candy bowl\. The contact lens was safe, we weren’t arrested, and the 1970s had delivered yet another unforgettable, true adventure\.
